thread:
alert-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: sudden 5xx spike tied to smart-routing fallbacks. metric=5xx_rate window=5m value=9.6% (baseline ~0.2%). routing policy 'cost-pref' matched a deprecated variant causing region fallback churn (eu-west -> us-east). auto-fallbacks & client retries creating amplification. Correlating logs and spike in outbound qps to us-east.

maria: ACK — paging @kevin @sam. Oncall here, starting triage. Can someone grab the routing /policy logs?

kevin: looking. I see match rule that unintentionally includes quantized variants: `match: model_variant =~ "gpt-.*-quant"` — that's wrong, should be restricted. Fallback policy set to "regional-failover" with no rate-limiting. Clients retrying immediately, so each failed request triggers a fallback that fans out to other regions.

sam: grabbing metrics now. Confirming thundering herd pattern: retries per client spiked 3x and because routing fallbacks are synchronous we're doubling requests to us-east. Also seeing increased KV cache misses in the hot region which explains latency spike.

maria: visible customer impact? jess, can you check support queue and top talkers?

jess: opened list — 3 high-traffic customers reporting increased errors and latency: AcmeCorp (chat), NimbusAI (batch embeddings), internal-test-org. I'll send an interim customer note once we have mitigation.

kevin: propose immediate mitigations:
1) disable the problematic fallback rule for policy 'cost-pref' in prod
2) enforce transient circuit-breaker on fallback path (short window) to stop retries from amplifying
3) patch rule to exclude quantized variants until we validate them

Commands I'm about to run (will post output):
```
# disable fallback policy quickly
redwoodctl routing policy update --name cost-pref --env prod --set fallback_enabled=false

# add circuit breaker (short term)
redwoodctl routing rule add --env prod --name fallback-circuit --match "fallback=true" --action throttle --rate 20rps
```

sam: agree. Also suggest adding a spike-protection header we can apply at the edge to drop excessive repeats: `x-rw-retry-serial` check. I'll open a quick filter rule in the edge proxy.

maria: go for the policy disable first. kevin, run that and share output. sam, start edge filter. jess, draft customer note: short blurb + ETA for fix.

kevin: running now:
```
> redwoodctl routing policy update --name cost-pref --env prod --set fallback_enabled=false
INFO: policy cost-pref updated (fallback_enabled=false)
> routing-config: propagating to 12 routing-nodes
```

kevin: I see propagation success to ~10/12 nodes; two nodes lagging but majority in effect. Confirming drop in fallback traffic in metrics (us-east qps down ~45% within 20s).

sam: edge filter rule in place:
```
edge-proxy> add-filter drop-if-header-retries > 5
OK: rule active
```

sam: also applied short-circuit on repeated retry patterns: any request with same client-retry-id seen >3 times in 10s now returns 429 upstream to avoid amplifying.

maria: nice. jess, send update to accounts now. Keep the note conservative: we mitigated fallback, mitigating retry amplification; customers may still see elevated latency while caches warm.

jess: sending now to impacted accounts and to the support channel. message: "We've mitigated a routing fallback issue that was amplifying client retries. You may see transient latency while caches rehydrate. We're monitoring and will follow up with a root-cause timeline." :white_check_mark:

robin: product note — we need to update rollout checks so model-variant matching rules are validated against a compatibility matrix. Creating a follow-up ticket.

kevin: follow-ups I'm pushing:
- patch policy rule to tighten variant match to explicit list
- add fallback rate-limits to all regional policies
- add a canary propagation guard that prevents simultaneous full-propagation when rule changes affect >N nodes

kevin: running patch now and will open PR; a quick live override applied already but will make the change permanent in config repo.

sam: monitoring dashboards: errors trending down, us-east qps stable. KV cache hit-rate recovering. No new spikes in the last 60s.

maria: handing off to on-call-sre for follow-up monitoring window. @sam you're primary for next 30m; I'll stay on until metrics look normal.

sam: taking it. I've updated incident status: mitigation applied, customer notifications sent, tracking follow-ups: rollback->config patch->postmortem. I'll file the incident ticket.

maria: final ask: include exact affected customers + delta in monthly report. jess, can you attach logs you collected to the ticket? Also include the exact CLI outputs for policy disable and edge rule changes.

jess: will attach screenshots and log snippets in the ticket.

robin: scheduling post-mortem for tomorrow 10am PT. We'll cover: policy validation gaps, fallback rate-limits, client retry guidance, and rollout propagation safeguards.

maria: thanks team. I'll close the page once sam confirms 30m stable window passed. Great quick action everyone. :pray:
